title: A figure citing a non-numeric fact passes untracedFigures
body:
## Summary
untracedFigures, the EraAdjusted props fact door, let a figure that cites a text column pass as traced and read a null fact as 0.

## Description
untracedFigures compared `Math.abs(Number(facts.get(key)) - value) > 1e-6` (packages/schemas/src/index.ts, before abf6a2e). A text fact becomes NaN, and no comparison with NaN is true, so the figure passed; a null or empty fact became a confident 0. ProjectService.setProps (apps/server/src/projects.ts:107) is the only door for co-pilot props, so a row citing e.g. a `#name` column was accepted as traced. This is the structured-output technique schema-validation-and-repair's 'missing values arrive as confident zeros'. Fixed: a fact counts only as a finite number or a numeric string (packages/schemas/src/index.ts:191); anything else is reported with the key and the observed value. Parity note (out of scope): apps/server/src/projects.ts writeScript skips string facts entirely (`typeof f === "number"`), while apps/server/src/generation/facts.ts handles them explicitly.

## Flow
- co-pilot calls set_props with raw_fact_key pointing at a text column
- wh.facts returns the string
- untracedFigures: Number('Juan Manuel Fangio') = NaN, NaN > 1e-6 is false -> no problem
- props version stored as traced

## Expected impact
Every EraAdjusted video's fact binding (ADR 003 #2). Could break: a fact the driver returns as a non-numeric object would now be refused (none observed: normalizeValue turns DuckDB objects into strings, which parse when numeric).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a figure is traced only by a numeric fact
Before: text fact -> 0 problems (silent pass); null fact read as 0
After: text / null / empty fact -> 1 problem each naming the key and value; a numeric string still traces (126 tests green)
Method: gate - red-then-green unit test
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: schemas.test.ts 'refuses a figure citing a fact that is not a number' (seeded red before the fix)

title: Reject a fixed DataRace axis_max below the largest value
body:
## Summary
A fixed axis_max lower than the data's peak drew every larger bar at the same full width with different labels; the schema accepted it.

## Description
Handed over from Compositions & Timing (Lane B, out-of-scope seam). axisMaxAt returns props.axis_max unchanged (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:138) and BarRow clamps value / axisMax to 1 (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/parts.tsx:157). The superRefine (packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:246) now rejects axis_max below the peak, naming the value and the entity. Golden path: data-video-art-direction anti-pattern 'the trick axis'; structured-output schema-validation-and-repair step 4 (invariants).

## Flow
- props set axis_max 70 over data peaking at 74
- bars above 70 all render full width
- two leaders look tied while their labels differ

## Expected impact
Viewers of a race with a hand-set cap. Could break: props that cap below their data (now refused with the fix in the message); none of the 53 props in the checkout set axis_max.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no bar is clipped by a fixed axis
Before: axis_max 70 over a peak of 74 accepted
After: rejected at axis_max with the observed peak and entity; 74 and 100 accepted; 53 of 53 real props still parse
Method: gate - red-then-green unit test, plus the 53-file population re-parsed
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: generation-rules.test.ts 'rejects a fixed axis_max below the largest value' (seeded red)

title: The axis_max comment says the axis follows the leader; it is grow-only
body:
## Summary
The comment on DataRace axis_max described the leader-following axis that 60606dc replaced with a grow-only max-so-far axis.

## Description
Handed over from Compositions & Timing (Lane B). Premise corrected at build: the sentence is a JSDoc comment, not a zod .describe(), so it never reached the model - the committed packages/compositions/fixtures/data-race-props.schema.json holds 0 description keys and packages/schemas has 0 .describe() calls. The card's 'could break: fixture regen' therefore did not apply. The comment (packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:197) now states the grow-only axis and the new >= peak rule, matching packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:129-136.

## Flow
- an author reads the field comment
- believes the axis rescales with the leader
- sets axis_max to stop a rescale that no longer happens

## Expected impact
Authors reading the schema source. Could break: nothing (comment only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the field comment states the rule the composition applies
Before: 1 sentence asserting a removed behaviour
After: 0
Method: probe - grep before and after; the rung above (a test) cannot pin prose that never ships
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
before: packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:188 /** fixed axis maximum; omit for an axis that follows the current leader */
grep -c '"description"' packages/compositions/fixtures/data-race-props.schema.json -> 0
instrument: grep for the stale sentence (1 -> 0) and for description keys in the JSON fixture (0)

title: extraArgs may override the session, prompt, model, budget or load plugins
body:
## Summary
extraArgsProblem's owned-flag list covered 13 of the CLI's flags and missed plugins, agents, browser and remote bridges, session swaps, the system prompt, the output stream, the model and the budget cap.

## Description
cli.extraArgs are appended after the runner's own flags (apps/server/src/generation/claude.ts:70), so a later flag overrides or widens what buildClaudeArgs set. The gate at config load (packages/schemas/src/generation.ts:72) refused --permission-mode, --add-dir, --mcp-config, --tools and similar, but `claude --help` (checked 2026-10-04) also offers --plugin-dir / --plugin-url (plugins carry hooks that run commands), --agents, --setting-sources, --permission-prompt-tool, --chrome, --ide, --remote-control, --cloud, --environment, --worktree, --tmux, --file, --debug-file, --resume / --continue / --session-id, --system-prompt / --append-system-prompt, --output-format (the runner parses stream-json), --model, --fallback-model and --max-budget-usd (the Q7 cap). Short forms (-r, -c, -w) were never checked. No registry technique governs the CLI flag surface; judged on SPEC D.5 ('extraArgs ... must not widen the sandbox') and the argv builder as ground truth.

## Flow
- owner config sets cli.extraArgs ['--plugin-dir', 'x'] or ['--max-budget-usd', '999']
- config load accepts it
- buildClaudeArgs appends it after the runner's flags
- the job loads a plugin or runs past the configured budget

## Expected impact
Generation job confinement and spend. Could break: an owner config that already uses one of these flags now fails to load with the flag named (no such config in the repo; SPEC D.5 example uses []).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the config gate refuses every flag the runner owns
Before: 0 of 33 refused
After: 33 of 33 refused; --effort, --betas, --autocompact still allowed
Method: gate - red-then-green it.each test against the flags `claude --help` lists
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: pipeline.test.ts it.each over 33 argument lists (all red before) + an allowed-flags case

title: Reject a negative DataRace value instead of drawing a 6 px stub
body:
## Summary
DataRace values accepted any finite number; a negative value rendered as a 6 px positive stub beside a negative label.

## Description
BarRow draws Math.max(6, Math.min(1, value / axisMax) * barMaxW) (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/parts.tsx:157) and runningMax floors at 0 (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts), so a bar race cannot show a value below zero. Each value now refines to >= 0 with the value in the message (packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:115). Golden path: data-video-art-direction 'the trick axis: broken bars'; structured-output step 2 (domain).

## Flow
- a series of net values (trade balance) goes below zero
- props pass the schema
- the bar shows a 6 px stub with '-3.5' beside it

## Expected impact
Any race over a signed quantity. Could break: such races are now refused at validation (0 of 53 real props carry a negative).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no bar contradicts its own label
Before: values[4] = -3.5 accepted
After: rejected at entities.2.values.4 with the value; 0 accepted; 53 of 53 real props still parse; JSON schema fixture unchanged
Method: gate - red-then-green unit test plus the population re-parse
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:115 .refine((v) => v >= 0, (v) => ({ message: `value ${v} is below 0: ...` }))
packages/compositions/src/DataRace/parts.tsx:157 const w = Math.max(6, Math.min(1, row.value / axisMax) * L.barMaxW);

title: EraAdjusted props accept unknown focus ids and duplicate player or scene ids
body:
## Summary
EraAdjustedPropsSchema checked highlight_player_id and nothing else; the DataRace schema checks every id it names.

## Description
Slopegraph dims every line not in a non-empty focus set (packages/viz/src/Slopegraph.tsx:63-75), so one focus id that names no row dims the whole chart for that scene; duplicate player_id rows collide on the per-id keys (Slopegraph.tsx:108); duplicate scene ids share one timing entry (packages/compositions/src/timing.ts:51). The refinement (packages/schemas/src/index.ts:163-178) now reports each with the observed id and the first occurrence, the rule DataRacePropsSchema already applies. Technique: structured-output schema-validation-and-repair step 3 (references).

## Flow
- co-pilot writes focus ['fangio'] for the reveal scene
- set_props accepts it
- the reveal scene renders every line dimmed

## Expected impact
EraAdjusted renders. Could break: props with such ids are refused; the paid LLM replay fixture's set_props props and sampleEraProps still parse, and data/app.sqlite holds 0 stored props rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every id the props name resolves
Before: 3 of 3 cases accepted
After: 3 of 3 rejected with path and observed id; replay props unaffected
Method: gate - red-then-green tests plus a probe of the paid replay props
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: schemas.test.ts 'references resolve' (2 tests, seeded red); paid replay props re-parsed

title: Drop the unused Script words_per_minute (a third, stale narration rate)
body:
## Summary
ScriptSchema defaulted words_per_minute to 140-175 wpm while the word budget uses the measured 115-128 wpm; nothing read the schema field.

## Description
rg 'words_per_minute' over the tracked tree (e2e fixtures included) hit only packages/schemas/src/index.ts. The budget writeScript enforces is NARRATOR_WPM = {115,128} (apps/server/src/projects.ts:63); DESIGN.md:384 says 150-165. The schema carried a contradicting second authority (structured-output: one-authority-per-vocabulary). Removed; a stored script with the key still parses (key dropped).

## Flow
- a reader trusts the parsed script's words_per_minute
- plans a 60 s narration at 175 wpm
- writeScript rejects it as too long at the measured 128 wpm

## Expected impact
Low: removes a misleading number. Could break: nothing reads it (zero-consumer grep).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one narration rate
Before: parsed scripts carry {140,175}; 0 consumers
After: absent; 0 consumers; old scripts parse
Method: gate - red-then-green test plus the zero-consumer grep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
rg words_per_minute (tracked, excluding data/): packages/schemas/src/index.ts:233 only (before 3f624dd; the line is gone)
apps/server/src/projects.ts:63 export const NARRATOR_WPM = { min: 115, max: 128 };
instrument: schemas.test.ts 'carries no narration rate of its own' (seeded red); zero-consumer rg

title: Every text and list limit names the field and how many fit
body:
## Summary
Six limits still answered with zod's default 'String must contain at most 4 character(s)', naming neither field nor remedy.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:77-80 declares one wording for every length limit and array cap, but value_format.prefix (4) and .suffix (6), an event card's facts (2), spotlight.facts (2), EraAdjusted title (60) and scene on_screen (80) used zod's default. The generation loop and the co-pilot retry on these messages (structured-output: 'feedback must be actionable by the model'). Not changed: entities > 10 is still reported by both the schema and rule 3.

## Flow
- the model writes suffix ' M/year'
- the validator returns 'String must contain at most 6 character(s)'
- the retry guesses which field and how short

## Expected impact
Generation and co-pilot retries. Could break: tests matching the old default wording (none).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every limit's message names the field and the remedy
Before: 6 of 6 overflows answered with the default wording
After: 6 of 6 use the shorten-it / drop-some wording; JSON schema fixture unchanged
Method: gate - red-then-green tests
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:147 .max(2, tooMany("facts on one card", 2))
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:193 prefix: z.string().max(4, tooLong("value prefix", 4))
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:94 on_screen: z.string().max(80, eraTooLong("on_screen", 80))
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:140 title: z.string().max(60, eraTooLong("title", 60))
instrument: generation-rules.test.ts 'uses the same wordings ...' and schemas.test.ts 'title and scene text ...' (seeded red)

title: Bump TIMING_PLAN_VERSION after the last-period crown change
body:
## Summary
0eb3254 changed what the plan's last order means (the crown is the largest final value) without bumping TIMING_PLAN_VERSION, so a stored v1 plan from before could re-render the old crown.

## Description
TIMING_PLAN_VERSION stays 1 (packages/schemas/src/timing-plan.ts:11) although computeTimingPlan's last-period order changed. A version bump would make every stored plan 'not supported - recompute the plan' (and recomputing changes the sha the props name). Measured whether any stored plan actually disagrees with its props before proposing it.

## Flow
- re-render an old generation job from its stored plan
- the ending crowns plan.orders[last][0]
- compare with the largest final value in its props

## Expected impact
None measured. A bump would invalidate every stored plan for re-render.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stored plans never crown a different entity than the data
Before: 0 of 42 stored props (data/generation, 5 legacy plans without orders skipped) crown a different entity than their largest final value
After: 0 of 42 with a bump - same figure, plus every stored plan invalidated
Method: probe - script over the stored plans and props
Result: not-better
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
probe over data/generation/*/work/out: props checked 42, crown mismatch 0, plans without orders 5 (pre-T9 legacy, version undefined)
packages/schemas/src/timing-plan.ts:11 export const TIMING_PLAN_VERSION = 1;
instrument: stored plans in data/generation: last order[0] vs argmax of final values

title: Rule 4 reveal check matches only the winner's full name, not a surname
body:
## Summary
checkGenerationRules rule 4 flags a title or hook only when it contains the winner's full name, its id with spaces, or a model-supplied alias, so a surname or an unaccented spelling reveals the winner unchecked.

## Description
names = [winner.name, winner.id with '-' -> ' ', ...aliases] (packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:243) and containsTerm needs the whole phrase (generation-rules.ts:74-79) and is accent-sensitive. 'Can Hamilton hold on?' for winner 'Lewis Hamilton' and 'Will Perez hold on?' for 'Sergio Pérez' pass unless the model listed the alias itself. SPEC D.8 rule 4: 'Neither may contain the name of the final #1 entity'. data-video-art-direction anti-pattern 'the spoiler title'. The fix needs a token rule (surname / distinctive tokens, NFKD-folded) whose false-positive rate on short brand names ('Red' in 'Red Bull') must be measured first.

## Flow
- the plan crowns Lewis Hamilton
- the model writes hook 'Can Hamilton hold on?' with no aliases
- rule 4 passes; the first two seconds name the winner

## Expected impact
Every DataRace title/hook on a person race. Could break: false positives on common name tokens (the reason this needs its instrument).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a title cannot name the final #1 by surname
Before: simulation: 3 walked cases (Hamilton surname; Pérez unaccented; an F1 2010 hook 'Vettel's year?') pass rule 4
After: predicted: all 3 flagged; false positives unknown until counted
Method: simulation - the token rule's false-positive count needs the population harness; the 53-file population holds only ~5 distinct titles, too few to decide alone
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:243 const names = winner ? [str(winner.name), str(winner.id).replace(/-/g, " "), ...arr(winner.aliases).map(str)] : [];
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:77 const re = new RegExp(`(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])${escapeRe(t)}(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])`, "iu");
instrument: rule-4 cases in generation-rules.test.ts ('Can Hamilton hold on?' for winner 'Lewis Hamilton'; accent-folded 'Perez' for 'Sergio Pérez') red, plus a false-positive count of the token rule over every title/hook in the 53-file props population

title: Rule 3 colour uniqueness compares exact hex; lookalike colours pass
body:
## Summary
Every entity needs a unique colour, but rule 3 only rejects identical hex strings; 13 of 53 real props carry a pair 14 RGB units apart.

## Description
rule3 keys a Map by the lowercased hex (packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:171-181). data/generation/gj-18c8a1b5 v3 gives Quill #a47148 and Prism #9c6644 - two near-identical browns. data-video-art-direction anti-pattern 'lookalike identities'; SPEC D.8 rule 3 'every entity gets a unique colour'. Tightening rejects existing outputs, so the threshold must be measured on the population before it is pinned.

## Flow
- the visual_options session picks a brown palette
- two entities differ by a few RGB units
- rule 3 passes; viewers cannot tell two bars apart

## Expected impact
Readability of every race. Could break: today's outputs - 13 of 53 props would fail at a distance-14 threshold.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - entity colours are distinguishable, not merely different strings
Before: probe: nearest-pair RGB distance 14 in 13 of 53 props, 33 in 13, 47 in 27 (exact-hex rule: 0 rejected)
After: unknown until a threshold is chosen against the population
Method: probe - population script; the threshold is the A/B question
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:180 if (prev) add("duplicate-colour", ...)
probe min colour distances (53 props): 14 x13, 33 x13, 47 x27
data/generation/gj-18c8a1b5/work/out/variants/v3.props.json Quill #a47148 vs Prism #9c6644
instrument: a perceptual-distance threshold (e.g. CIEDE2000) run over the 53-file props population: count rejects at each threshold, then a rule-3 test pinning the chosen one

title: props_schema handed to the generation model carries no field descriptions
body:
## Summary
Every field rule in data-race.ts is a JSDoc comment, so get_generation_context's props_schema reaches the model with 0 descriptions.

## Description
zod-to-json-schema emits descriptions only from .describe(); packages/schemas has 0 .describe() calls and the committed packages/compositions/fixtures/data-race-props.schema.json has 0 description keys. GENERATION_RULES (apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:58-67) restates rules 1-6 in words, but axis_max, the null meaning of values, value_format, unit_label and source_line reach the model as bare types. structured-output: one-authority-per-vocabulary - the prompt should be rendered from the same definitions the door enforces.

## Flow
- get_generation_context returns props_schema
- the model sees axis_max: number > 0 and nothing else
- it copies the plan's strategy.axis_max into props, or omits values semantics

## Expected impact
Live generation quality. Could break: the JSON schema fixture (regen), token count of the context call.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the schema the model reads carries the field rules the validator enforces
Before: 0 described fields of ~30
After: predicted ~30 described; behavioural effect unmeasured
Method: probe - grep of the fixture and the source; the build is M with a director-owned fixture regen
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: count of DataRace fields with a description in dataRacePropsJsonSchema() (0 today) after converting the JSDoc to .describe(); regenerate packages/compositions/fixtures/data-race-props.schema.json with `WRITE_FIXTURES=1 npx vitest run packages/compositions/src/DataRace/write-fixtures.test.ts`; the behavioural figure (fewer validator retries per live job) needs paid generation runs and is operator-only

title: caseStage reads a done generate_video job with no video as visuals_ready
body:
## Summary
For visuals, 'done without producing a variant' is visuals_failed; for video, 'done without a videos row' falls through to visuals_ready, as if the generate step had not run.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/pipeline.ts:34 maps only failed/cancelled video jobs to video_failed; a done job with ctx.videos 0 reaches `if (accepted) return "visuals_ready"` (pipeline.ts:37), while the visual branch says `if (visuals) return "visuals_failed"; // failed, cancelled, or done without producing a variant` (pipeline.ts:42). The worker records the video in finalize before 'done' (apps/server/src/generation/worker.ts:279-281), so the state is reached when finalize registered no video (fake mode, a deleted row). The studio badge for video_failed reads the job (apps/studio/src/board/jobs.ts:145) and needs a matching label - another context.

## Flow
- generate_video finishes 'done' but no videos row exists for the case
- caseStage returns visuals_ready
- the board shows the case waiting on a generate step that already ran

## Expected impact
Board state honesty. Could break: the studio badge copy for this state.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for 'a job done without its output' across both job types
Before: simulation: done + 0 videos -> visuals_ready
After: predicted video_failed with a retry action
Method: simulation - the stage test is S but the badge seam is in apps/studio (out of scope)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: pipeline.test.ts caseStage case: accepted item + generate_video 'done' + videos 0 (expected video_failed), plus the studio badge for that stage (apps/studio/src/board/jobs.ts:145) - out-of-scope seam

title: Event-title 'never the final ranking' rule is claimed but unenforced
body:
## Summary
data-race.ts says event titles 'never [name] the final ranking (rule 4; checked by checkGenerationRules)', but rule 4 only checks event titles for newlines.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:140 comment and SPEC D.8 rule 4 ('Event card titles ... may name entities but never the final ranking'); rule4 (packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:253-256) only adds event-title-multiline. Either the check is built (winner name with a reveal word in a card title) or the comment stops claiming it. An event about a mid-race win must stay legal, so the rule needs its false-positive count.

## Flow
- a card titled 'Juniper takes the crown' appears mid-race
- rule 4 passes it
- the race's ending is spoiled before the ending

## Expected impact
Spoilers in event cards. Could break: legitimate mid-race event titles if the rule is too broad.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stated rule and the check agree
Before: simulation: a card naming the final #1 with 'takes the crown' passes; population 0 of 11 titles would trip a winner+denylist rule
After: predicted: flagged with 0 false positives on the population
Method: simulation - population too small to decide; needs the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:140 /** <= 36 chars, one line ...; may name entities, never the final ranking (rule 4; checked by checkGenerationRules) */
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:255 if (/[\r\n]/.test(t)) add("event-title-multiline", ...)
instrument: a rule-4 event-title case (winner name + a reveal word in events[i].title) red, plus a false-positive count over every event title in the props population (11 distinct today, 0 hits)

title: life_frames 105-135 lives only in rule 6, not in the schema or its JSON
body:
## Summary
DataRaceEventSchema types life_frames as any integer; only checkGenerationRules rule 6 enforces 105-135, so schema-only parsers and the JSON schema the model reads accept 0 or 10000.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:151 life_frames: z.number().int().optional(); rule6 (packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:284) holds the range. Schema-only doors (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/DataRace.tsx:16, Remotion Studio's props editor via packages/compositions/src/Root.tsx:54) accept any integer, and the JSON schema has no minimum/maximum. structured-output enumerable-domain-decoding: 'the same field is validated in three places'. Not built this round: M, touches the rule-6 contract tests and the director-owned fixture for a small gain (the validator already rejects out-of-range values before render).

## Flow
- an author edits life_frames to 0 in Remotion Studio
- the schema accepts it
- the card never appears

## Expected impact
Small: render-time props already passed rule 6. Could break: the JSON fixture (regen) and rule-6 tests (strengthened).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one door for the card lifespan
Before: probe: 3 doors, 1 enforces the range; JSON schema minimum/maximum absent
After: predicted: schema enforces it, rule 6 defers, JSON carries 105-135
Method: probe - read of the three doors; build deferred for size
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:151 life_frames: z.number().int().optional(),
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:288 if (typeof life !== "number" || ... life < DATA_RACE_LIMITS.lifeFramesMin || life > DATA_RACE_LIMITS.lifeFramesMax)
instrument: move the range to DataRaceEventSchema (.min(105).max(135) with the tooLong-style wording), make rule 6 defer like rule 4 defers title length (one violation, not two), strengthen the rule-6 tests, regenerate the JSON schema fixture with `WRITE_FIXTURES=1 npx vitest run packages/compositions/src/DataRace/write-fixtures.test.ts` (DataRace.test.tsx:70 fails without it)

title: The script pronunciation ledger (ADR 003 #7) is accepted but never applied
body:
## Summary
ScriptSchema accepts pronunciations (packages/schemas/src/index.ts:235) and ADR 003 #7 decided a pronunciation ledger, but no code reads it: TTS speaks the token's spoken form only.

## Description
rg 'pronunciations' over the tracked tree hits only packages/schemas/src/index.ts and the sample fixture (packages/schemas/src/fixtures.ts:46). DESIGN.md:326 promises a ledger. A co-pilot that writes { 'Räikkönen': 'RYE-koh-nen' } believes the name will be said that way. Both ways out need the owner: wiring it into the audio stage re-keys the paid audio fixtures; dropping the field reverses an ADR.

## Flow
- co-pilot writes a pronunciation entry
- write_script stores it
- the audio stage never reads it; the name is mispronounced

## Expected impact
EraAdjusted narration (legacy M1 path; ADR 007 videos have no narration). Could break: audio replay fixtures.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ledger the ADR decided either works or is gone
Before: 1 accepted field, 0 consumers
After: owner call: wire it (paid re-record) or drop it (ADR change)
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep; the decision is operator-only
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
rg pronunciations (tracked, excluding data/): packages/schemas/src/index.ts:235, packages/schemas/src/fixtures.ts:46 only
docs/decisions/003-media-generation-knowledge-review.md:20 '#7 ... plus a pronunciation ledger'
instrument: operator-only: applying the ledger changes TTS input text, which re-keys the paid audio replay fixtures (e2e/fixtures/audio, ElevenLabs re-record); removing the field contradicts ADR 003 #7

title: @statreel/schemas declares yaml with zero imports
body:
## Summary
packages/schemas/package.json lists yaml ^2.8.0 but no file in the package imports it.

## Description
git ls-files packages/schemas lists 16 files; rg 'yaml' over packages/schemas/src finds 0 imports. The registry YAML is read by apps/server, which declares its own yaml dependency (apps/server/package.json:20). The schemas package is also bundled into the studio and the Remotion bundle (packages/schemas/src/sha256.ts:2-3), so its declared dependencies should be the ones it uses.
